verdictRationale: DONE_CURRENT_SHA at testedSha 05cf060f67. The repository-owned PARTIAL_SIGKILL blocker is closed without trusting caller-controlled correlation: every request receives a server-generated UUID, returned as x-request-id, and an authenticated denial with canonical tenant plus actor is not put on the wire until the durable repair intent commits under that server identity. Timeout or failure destroys the socket instead of acknowledging a denial whose intent may be lost. An unauthenticated 401 without tenant/actor remains an in-process non-tenant operational metric and is not misrepresented as a tenant durable intent. Exact-current unit and mounted signed-JWT real-PostgreSQL gates pass with zero run-owned residue and zero advisory locks; the predecessor lifecycle/concurrency qualification remains valid because the product successor changes only the request identity fence and its tests. AMD-OBSERVABILITY-INTERNAL-GATE-002 classifies external paging and deployed observation as release gates, so they do not block repository technical DONE and remain unclaimed.

supersededRepositoryBlocker.historical: PARTIAL_SIGKILL: an accepted authenticated denial could be acknowledged before its durable intent completed.
supersededRepositoryBlocker.current: RESOLVED. metricsMiddleware creates a server-owned per-request UUID, returns it as x-request-id and uses it for authenticated tenant denial durability; a reused client x-request-id cannot collapse distinct requests. It delays res.end until the durable intent barrier settles. On timeout or failure it destroys the socket, so the application never acknowledges a denial whose durable intent is not known to have committed.
